title: Prove a signed-out or expired session cannot be reused

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0059 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive to advance the remaining uncited acceptance criteria. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0059.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: AC-004's 'the session cannot be reused' clause was proven only via client cookie removal: the logout HTTP 401 was equally explained by the supertest agent dropping the cleared cookie, and expiry was proven only at the AuthService tier, so server-side invalidation was unobserved through HTTP. AuthService.logout deletes the session and authenticateSession rejects an expired session, but that path had no HTTP-tier proof.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts logout and authenticateSession, and the prior coverage audit of AC-004.

claims.statement: The change adds an HTTP-tier proof that a pre-logout token value replayed on a fresh request, and a token replayed after its TTL elapses, are both rejected by the server with 401 — distinguishing server invalidation from client cookie removal. No product code changes; the capability already existed.

Governed discovery reordered the work: AC-004's gap was a missing proof, not a missing capability, so the slice adds a test that replays the token value on a fresh request rather than changing the server.
claims.evidence: Governed-discovery reorder check on 2026-08-24 and the AuthService invalidation paths.

claims.statement: Replaying the pre-logout token value on a fresh request and asserting 401, plus rejecting a token replayed past its TTL via an injected clock, proves AC-004's server-side invalidation.
claims.evidence: server/tests/unit/sessionInvalidation.test.ts is the falsification mechanism; while the session is live the same replayed token authenticates (200), so the 401 is attributable to invalidation.

claims.statement: AC-013 (runtime edits never alter a saved Scene without an explicit save-back, at the persistence tier) and AC-016 (a device token executes only its selected actions, surfaced through the Integrations UI) remain uncited by a change contract and are deferred.
claims.evidence: SPEC-0001 AC-013 and AC-016 and the coverage-denominator of uncited acceptance criteria.

successCriteria.statement: A pre-logout session token replayed on a fresh request after sign-out is rejected with 401, while the same token authenticated with 200 before sign-out.
successCriteria.verification: Focused HTTP test replays the captured token before and after logout.

successCriteria.statement: A session token replayed after its TTL elapses is rejected with 401.
successCriteria.verification: Focused HTTP test with an injected clock advances past the session TTL and replays the token.

successCriteria.statement: No product code changes and no existing behavior regresses.
successCriteria.verification: Path-scoped review that only server/tests and governance changed; the full server suite passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0059 records the AC-004 server-invalidation proof and the remaining uncited AC-013 and AC-016 before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: An HTTP-tier test proves replayed-token rejection after logout and after expiry, attributable to the server.
The test passes and the full server suite passes.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit and git diff --check.
